text: Git branching is an important part of the version control workflow. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. This is why developers create feature branches for each task. When the work is finished, you can combine it with the main project through merging. Before that happens, many teams use pull requests so others can review the changes and give feedback. This process keeps the code stable and helps teams work together. Understanding branches, merging, and pull requests makes collaboration easier and reduces mistakes in a project.
